'''Arts and culture'''
*The Finnish city of [[Oulu]] is chosen as the [[European Capital of Culture]] for 2026. [https://yle.fi/uutiset/osasto/news/oulu_named_2026_european_capital_of_culture/11961818 (''Yle Uutiset'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Pacific typhoon season]]
**[[Tropical Storm Choi-wan (2021)|Tropical Storm Choi-wan (Dante)]] makes [[landfall]] in central and southern [[Philippines]], killing at least three people and leaving hundreds displaced. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/storm-leaves-3-dead-displaces-hundreds-in-philippines/2021/06/02/06953578-c37e-11eb-89a4-b7ae22aa193e_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*The [[Iranian Navy]] replenishment and training ship {{ship|IRIS|Kharg}} catches fire and sinks at [[Jask]], [[Hormozgan Province|Hormozgan]], Iran. It was the largest vessel in their fleet. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-navy-training-ship-fire-mouth-gulf-crew-evacuated-report-2021-06-01/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 126 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, which is the first time that daily deaths exceeded 100. This thereby brings the nationwide [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death toll]] to 2,993. [https://themalaysianreserve.com/2021/06/02/covid-19-malaysia-records-7703-cases/ (The Malaysian Reserve)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Vietnam]] reverses an international flight suspension imposed in [[Hanoi]]'s [[Noi Bai International Airport]], which was originally supposed to end on June 7, and in [[Ho Chi Minh City]]'s [[Tan Son Nhat International Airport]], which was originally supposed to end on June 14. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/vietnam-reverses-covid-19-flight-suspension-in-hanoi-and-ho-chi-minh (''The Straits Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in France]]
****[[President of France|President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] announces that [[France|French]] teenagers aged 12 to 18 years old will be eligible for [[COVID-19 vaccine]] beginning from June 15 as the country reaches milestone of 50% of the adult population vaccinated with a first dose. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210602-france-to-offer-covid-19-vaccines-to-12-18-age-group-from-june-15-macron-says (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****The [[Spain|Spanish]] [[Government of Spain|government]] and regional authorities agree to allow bars and nightclubs to reopen for the first time in 10 months, with these establishments on [[Regions of Spain|regions]] with below 50 case rate per 100,000 population over 14 days can be open until 3:00 a.m. with 50% capacity. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/06/02/us-health-coronavirus-spain (Euronews)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mauritius]]
***[[Mauritius]] approves the usage of the single-dose [[Sputnik Light]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/russias-sputnik-light-vaccine-approved-use-mauritius-rdif-2021-06-02/ (Reuters)] 

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 United States Capitol attack]]
**Paul Allard Hodgkins, a [[Tampa, Florida|Tampa]] man who was seen in the [[United States Senate chamber|U.S. Senate chamber]] during the [[2021 United States Capitol attack|January 6 riot]] at the [[United States Capitol]], pleads guilty, making him the second suspect to do so after [[Jon Schaffer]]. [https://www.politico.com/news/2021/06/02/capitol-riot-defendant-pleads-guilty-491604 (''Politico'')]
*[[Steamship Authority cyberattack]]
**A [[ransomware]] attack affects [[Steamship Authority]], the ferry service between the mainland of [[Massachusetts]] and the islands of [[Martha's Vineyard]] and [[Nantucket]]. [https://apnews.com/article/massachusetts-technology-business-e0fdaff6384d90ed0f1ab2491e376803 (Associated Press)]
*According to a spokesperson for the independence movement, the leader of the [[Polisario Front]], [[Brahim Ghali]], arrived safely in [[Algiers]], Algeria. Ghali, who was hospitalized due to COVID-19 in [[Spain]], left the country after Spanish authorities refused to hold him in custody. The move angered [[Morocco]] due to Algeria's support of the Polisario Front. [https://www.reuters.com/article/spain-morocco-polisario/update-1-western-sahara-independence-leader-lands-in-algiers-amid-diplomatic-row-idUSL5N2NK19Z (Reuters)]
*[[CEO]]s of several [[South Korea]]n companies ask [[President of South Korea|President]] [[Moon Jae-in]] to pardon [[Samsung]]'s chairman [[Lee Jae-yong (businessman)|Lee Jae-yong]], who was sentenced to 30 months' imprisonment for [[bribery]], [[embezzlement]] and other offences. Moon did not elaborate but had said in March that he would consider public opinion. Before taking office in 2017, Moon had said that he would not pardon those convicted of serious economic crimes. [https://www.reuters.com/business/koreas-business-leaders-call-moon-free-jailed-samsung-boss-lee-2021-06-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[Nicaragua]]n opposition figure [[Cristiana Chamorro Barrios]] is placed under [[house arrest]] in [[Managua]] as the [[Government of Nicaragua|government]] accuses her of [[money laundering]]. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/world/2126163/nicaraguan-opposition-presidential-hopeful-chamorro-under-house-arrest (''Bangkok Post'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of Israel]]
**[[2019–2021 Israeli political crisis]]
***[[Yair Lapid]], leader of the [[Yesh Atid]] and [[Leader of the Opposition (Israel)|opposition]], informs outgoing [[President of Israel|President]] [[Reuven Rivlin]] that he and [[Yamina]] leader [[Naftali Bennett]] have reached a deal to form a [[coalition government]], which will remove [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] from power. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/lapid-informs-president-he-can-form-government-removing-netanyahu-from-power/ (''The Times of Israel'')] 
***[[Mansour Abbas]], leader of the [[United Arab List]] party, agrees to join the coalition. This is the first time in [[History of Israel|Israel's history]] that an [[Arab citizens of Israel|Arab]] party will be part of the ruling [[government of Israel|government]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/2/israeli-parties-due-to-unveil-anti-netanyahu-coalition-live (Al Jazeera English)]
**[[2021 Israeli presidential election]]
***The [[Knesset]] elects [[Isaac Herzog]] as the 11th [[President of Israel|president]] of [[Israel]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/israeli-lawmakers-to-vote-for-next-figurehead-president/2021/06/02/dc7395fe-c360-11eb-89a4-b7ae22aa193e_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[Refugees of the Syrian civil war|Syrian refugees]] extend their [[sit-in]] protests in front of the [[Christiansborg Palace|Danish Parliament]] for a third week, protesting the [[Danish government]]'s decision in April to cancel the [[residency permit]]s for [[refugee]]s from the [[Damascus]] area. The government says that the region is safe for refugees to return to, while the protesters say otherwise. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/2/syrian-refugees-protest-against-denmarks-attempt-to-return-them (Al Jazeera English)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Twitter suspensions]]
**[[Twitter]] suspends the account of [[President of Nigeria|Nigerian President]] [[Muhammadu Buhari]] for 12 hours for posting a tweet invoking the violence of the [[Nigerian Civil War]], where he fought as a [[major general]], in his threats against the [[Biafra]]n [[separatist]] group [[Indigenous People of Biafra]] (IPOB). Authorities blame IPOB for a recent [[Insurgency in Southeastern Nigeria|series of attacks]] on [[government of Nigeria|government]] buildings in [[Rivers State]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/2/twitter-removes-nigerian-presidents-abusive-civil-war-post (Al Jazeera English)]
*[[NASA]] announces the selection of two new missions to [[Venus]], [[VERITAS (spacecraft)|VERITAS]] and [[DAVINCI+]], which will launch between 2028 and 2030. They will be the first American [[spacecraft]] sent to Venus since the [[Magellan (spacecraft)|''Magellan'' mission]] in 1989. The missions will focus on [[Mapping of Venus|mapping]] the [[Geology of Venus|surface of Venus]] and calculating the [[Atmosphere of Venus|atmosphere's composition]] to better understand Venus's geological history. [https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/science/nasa-plans-two-new-missions-venus-its-first-decades-2021-06-02/ (Reuters)] [https://www.npr.org/2021/06/02/1002627399/nasa-picks-twin-missions-to-visit-venus-earths-evil-twin (NPR)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 Kentucky Derby]]
**[[Kentucky Derby]] winner [[Medina Spirit]] tests positive for a second [[drug test]], and now faces disqualification. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/06/02/sports/horse-racing/kentucky-derby-medina-spirit-baffert.html (''The New York Times'')]
